name: Colonic Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Colonic Atresia

criteria.description: Neonatal intestinal obstruction symptoms including abdominal distension and failure to pass meconium
Radiographic evidence of colonic obstruction with absence of distal gas and dilated proximal colon
Surgical confirmation of colonic discontinuity or atretic segment
Histopathological exclusion of other causes of obstruction such as Hirschsprung disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neonatal intestinal obstruction symptoms plus radiologic evidence of colonic obstruction and surgical confirmation of atresia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and surgical; histopathology helps exclude mimics.

laboratory: Metabolic alkalosis or acidosis depending on obstruction severity
Elevated inflammatory markers if perforation or sepsis present
imaging: Abdominal X-ray showing dilated proximal colon with absence of distal gas
Contrast enema demonstrating colonic discontinuity or microcolon distal to atresia
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence predominates
other: Intraoperative visualization of colonic atresia confirming diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of ganglion cells on rectal biopsy
Delayed passage of meconium but with different radiologic pattern
No colonic discontinuity on imaging or surgery
Meconium impaction rather than anatomical atresia
Characteristic soap-bubble appearance on abdominal X-ray

redFlags: Progressive abdominal distension with bilious vomiting
Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth
Signs of bowel perforation or sepsis
references: Moore SW, et al. Colonic atresia: a review of 25 years' experience. Pediatr Surg Int. 2010.
Orphanet: Colonic atresia. Orphanet Report Series, Rare Diseases Collection, 2021.
Holcomb GW, et al. Ashcraft's Pediatric Surgery. 7th Edition. 2019.
